newsitem.title: FRANCE: Togo denies planning to send troops to Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Togo denies planning to send troops to Zaire.

text.p: Togo's Foreign Minister Pierre Koffi Panou denied on Tuesday that his country planned to send troops to help the Zairean government defeat Rwandan-backed rebels who have captured a swathe of eastern Zaire.

A senior Defence Ministry official in Kinshasa told Reuters on Monday that Togo, Morocco and Chad were prepared to send troops and equipment, and Egypt had also offered materials. He said Zaire had already chartered planes for the operation.
But Panou told Reuters during a private visit to Paris: "There are no Togolese troops preparing to leave for Zaire. We haven't even discussed it.
"There has been no such request to Togo. I would know about it. The president (Gnassingbe Eyadema) has not been approached."
Togolese troops took part in a 1977 intervention along with Moroccan soldiers to put down a rebellion by former Katangese gendarmes in Zaire's mineral-rich southern mining province of Shaba.
Eyadema is an old friend and ally of Zaire's President Mobutu Sese Seko. Both French-backed rulers have been in power more than 30 years.
